rules: Show a base rate only with its source, year, country and population, linked to the evidence ledger.
Where our wording differs from the source's, say 'a similar question'. Never imply the respondent answered the same question.
Prefer the respondent's country (D11). If none exists for their country, show one from another country and name it.
Figures marked approximate were read from published charts; display them with 'about'.
Re-check every figure against its source before launch and at each release; record the check date here.

items.text: about 4 in 10 Canadians said AI products and services have more benefits than drawbacks
16% of US adults expected AI to have a positive effect on society over the next 20 years, and 40% a negative one
items.source: Pew Research Center, Americans and AI

items.text: about 4 in 10 adults in Great Britain said AI products and services have more benefits than drawbacks
about half of Australians said AI products and services have more benefits than drawbacks
62% of Canadians expected AI to eliminate more jobs than it creates
half of US adults said they were more concerned than excited about AI in daily life; 10% were more excited
64% of US adults said AI is developing too fast; 8% said not fast enough
49% of Canadians wanted AI development slowed down, 24% wanted it as fast as possible, and 13% wanted it abandoned
In a similar question, 80% of US adults chose keeping safety rules even if development is slower; 9% chose developing as fast as possible
85% of Canadians said governments should regulate AI
58% of UK adults named an independent regulator among those who should be responsible for AI safety; 58% also named the companies developing it
items.source: Ada Lovelace Institute and Alan Turing Institute

items.text: 72% of US adults said independent experts should test AI before release
63% of UK adults said they were not comfortable with AI making decisions that affect their lives
items.source: Ada Lovelace Institute and Alan Turing Institute

items.text: In a similar question, 62% of UK adults favoured explanations or human decisions even at some cost to accuracy; 8% said accuracy mattered more
items.source: Ada Lovelace Institute and Alan Turing Institute

items.text: fewer than 1 in 10 US adults would let AI make the final call, unsupervised, on hiring, loans, admissions, parole or medical priority
77% of US adults said protecting US workers should be an extremely or very important priority for government on AI
78% of Canadians said AI threatens jobs
